notes: Sample telegram_users.json - who may talk to the bot. Copy to telegram_users.json and edit. The bot registers a person here the first time it sees them, with user_type 0; raising that number is the deliberate act that grants them anything.

'user_type' is a clearance level on the same 0-100 ladder the web console uses. A command in telegram_support_commands.json carries a 'command_type', and a person may run it only when their user_type is at least that number. 0 is 'known but may do nothing but read'; 100 is 'may take a machine down'.
'status' other than 'active' stops the person being served at all, which is how someone is switched off without losing the record that they existed.

The chat ids and names below are placeholders. A real user_id is a number Telegram assigns; you get it by having the person message the bot once and reading it back with the bot's own listing command.

telegram_users.note: Lead DBA. user_type 100 is the only level that may restart a host or patch an instance.
On-call DBA. May run the read-only reports and the level-50 operations (kill a session, start a job), not the level-100 ones.
Registered automatically the first time they messaged the bot. Level 0 until somebody decides otherwise - that default is the whole point.
